<description>
The multisig setup flows need to assemble a descriptor from collected cosigner keys without hand-crafting the descriptor string, which today means bash interpolation with no validation of key forms, duplicates, or threshold.

CreateMultisigDescriptor() takes a threshold, a list of key expressions with origin info, and an output type, and returns a ranged, multipath wsh(sortedmulti(...)) descriptor with checksum.

Part of the multisig wizard tracking issue #35645.
</description>

[2026-11-10] r:5838137065 review COMMENTED by fametrano (contributor):
Concept ACK

rxbryan wrote that the descriptor is built up front and becomes the source of truth for the setup, so I checked that string against code outside Core, on 589f3fe6b5. Over 98 cases (2 to 6 account xpubs with origin, every threshold, 49 per output type), Core's string equals the descriptor I expected, checksummed by bip32-descriptors, a library I maintain, in 98 of 98. The library derives the same receive and change scriptPubKeys at indexes 0 to 4: 980 of 980, 490 of them Taproot.

The string still depends on the order the keys come in: the six orders of the test's three keys give six descriptors and six checksums per output type, with the same scriptPubKeys, so cosigners who enter the keys in a different order get descriptors that do not compare equal. Sorting `canonical_keys` before assembly gave one descriptor for all six orders, scriptPubKeys unchanged. Could the keys be sorted, or the header say that the string depends on their order?

Gist: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/cc31cf590d6f7a977866849b1e67a998/3fb58384cdeb54184ce5f8599e351015c5d8a69e
